PullRequest.Title: Batch SVG whitespace markers in the editor per line
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #201123.

## Summary

- Batch SVG whitespace dots and tab arrows into one path per line containing markers instead of creating a separate DOM element for every character.
- Preserve marker geometry, theme colors, whitespace visibility modes, and the font/legacy rendering paths.
- Add 12 focused whitespace-overlay regression tests, including a constant SVG element-count assertion for a line containing 1,000 spaces.

Whitespace shares per-line HTML with selection highlights. Changing a selection replaces that line's overlay subtree, rebuilding otherwise unchanged SVG markers. Drag auto-scroll also forces the pending style/layout work when reading geometry for hit testing. The attached issue profile shows this DOM/style cost; enabling SVG whitespace by default also matches the reported 1.74.3 -> 1.75.1 regression boundary.

## Performance evidence

Measured in an isolated Code OSS 1.139.0 / Electron 42.10.0 window on Windows, with extensions disabled, the historical 1,992-line Rust file near line 140, `editor.renderWhitespace: all`, and 6x renderer CPU throttling. Selection used 90 real mouse updates ending in the same 2,109 selected characters. Scrolling used 120 wheel updates, 150 lines down and back.

| Metric | Original | Batched SVG | Original restored |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Glyph elements in the initial viewport | 778 | 49 | 778 |
| Selection: renderer task time | 16.48 s | 12.51 s | 17.51 s |
| Selection: style recalculation | 6.33 s | 3.35 s | 6.68 s |
| Selection: p95 inter-frame interval | 250 ms | 150 ms | 250 ms |
| Scrolling: style recalculation | 2.76 s | 1.91 s | 2.73 s |

All 778 whitespace markers remain present. Restoring the original implementation restores the style cost. Without CPU throttling, selection style time fell from 599 ms to 306 ms. An editor-content screenshot comparison found a maximum RGB-channel difference of 1/255 (antialiasing).

These are controlled local measurements with automation/recording overhead, not a claim to reproduce the reporter's exact Linux/Wayland hardware or physical battery-saver mode. Other renderer work remains; the change does not make every 6x-throttled frame meet a 60 Hz budget.

## Validation

- [x] `npm run gulp compile-client` (zero compilation errors)
- [x] Targeted hygiene, including formatting and ESLint, for both changed files
- [x] `scripts\test.bat`: 190 passing tests across whitespace overlay, view layer, and line renderer suites
- [x] Real Code OSS drag-selection, wheel-scrolling, and drag-auto-scroll scenarios
- [x] Live checks for spaces, tab arrows, all/boundary/trailing/none modes, partial selection and Select All

## Visual validation (Windows)

Ran the pre-PR whitespace renderer and the current implementation in the same Code OSS 1.139.0 / Electron 42.10.0 build, using fresh profiles and identical inputs/settings. Captured and visually reviewed all eight before/after image pairs. Used native Chromium viewport screenshots so non-default zoom is captured correctly; AI affordances were disabled in both test profiles to avoid transient selection-toolbar icons.

| Case | Markers before / after | Paths after | Maximum RGB-channel difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original Rust file, zoom -1 (~83%) | 927 / 927 | 58 | 4/255 |
| Original Rust file, zoom 0 (100%) | 778 / 778 | 48 | 1/255 |
| Original Rust file, zoom +1 (120%) | 662 / 662 | 40 | 4/255 |
| Original Rust file, zoom +2 (144%) | 543 / 543 | 32 | 9/255 |
| Wrapped Hebrew/Arabic/Latin with tabs | 191 / 191 | 20 | 2/255 |
| Wrapped RTL with a multi-line selection | 191 / 191 | 20 | 2/255 |
| Consolas with mixed fallback fonts and styled tokens | 210 / 210 | 20 | 2/255 |
| Proportional Georgia with fallback fonts and ligatures | 210 / 210 | 15 | 6/255 |

Every pair has matching marker counts, SVG glyph geometry, text-line bounds, selections, font styles, and actual platform-font sets. No missing/misaligned markers or new text shifts/clipping were observed. Images are not pixel-identical: remaining differences are small rasterization/antialiasing changes, at most 9/255 per RGB channel.

Zoom factors were checked in the renderer. Chromium's platform-font API confirmed real fallback fonts in the mixed-font cases, including Yu Gothic, Segoe UI Emoji, Courier New, Noto Sans KR, and Tahoma where needed, alongside regular/bold/italic Consolas or Georgia. Wrapping was also checked to produce more visual lines than model lines.

The review follow-up skips empty paths on marker-free lines. Consequently, the final default-zoom screenshot has **48 paths for all 778 markers**; the earlier timing runs above used 49 paths, including one empty path. Compilation, targeted hygiene, and **190 focused editor tests** pass on the follow-up commit.

This verifies the local Windows setup, not macOS/Linux or every font/display-scaling configuration. The PR remains a draft.

- [x] Local Windows visual validation at zoom levels -1/0/1/2, with wrapping/RTL and mixed font families
- [ ] Cross-platform visual validation on macOS and Linux

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The default SVG whitespace renderer created one SVG child element for every visible space or tab. Overlay line replacement on scrolling and selection-related rendering repeatedly constructed and destroyed a DOM subtree whose node count scaled with visible whitespace glyphs rather than visible lines.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Editors with renderWhitespace enabled and whitespace-dense visible lines incurred excessive synchronous DOM/style recalculation during scrolling and drag selection, causing increased renderer task time and frame delays.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added wrapper at whitespace.ts:234 emits the accumulated glyph geometry as a single SVG path per line, while _renderCircle and _renderArrow now return closed path-data subpaths. Rendering still scans and serializes each visible marker, but DOM element creation, attachment, style matching, and teardown shrink from one shape per whitespace glyph to at most one shape per rendered line.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, whitespace.ts:219 appends a separate <circle> for each visible space, while _renderArrow returns a separate <path> for each visible tab. _applyRenderWhitespace iterates every whitespace character of every visible line (bounded by stopRenderingLineAfter, whose default is 10,000), and SVG is the default experimentalWhitespaceRendering mode. ViewOverlays.prepareRender runs the overlay on invalidation, ViewOverlayLine concatenates its markup with the other overlays, and viewLayer applies changed line HTML through innerHTML, making all of those glyph nodes synchronous DOM/style work during visible-line rendering. The PR body provides controlled editor measurements showing 778 glyph elements before versus 49 per-line paths after and corresponding reductions in selection and scrolling style-recalculation time.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or vertically scroll an editor with SVG whitespace rendering enabled and renderWhitespace set to all, boundary, or trailing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On initial render and vertical scrolling, WhitespaceOverlay.prepareRender synchronously scans each visible line, resolves each rendered whitespace position, builds SVG markup, and ViewOverlayLine/viewLayer may commit changed line HTML via innerHTML before the frame completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize whitespace SVG markup and parse/attach it into the editor overlay DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one SVG child shape was parsed and materialized per visible whitespace glyph; after the diff, one SVG path child is materialized per visible line containing markers. Position lookup and path-data serialization remain once per marker. Effective cardinality is bounded by visible lines and stopRenderingLineAfter (default 10,000 characters per line).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same critical-path DOM boundary existed, but each whitespace marker produced its own <circle> or <path> child; the diff reduces this to one child path per marker-bearing line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: DOM parsing, node construction, style matching, and attachment occur synchronously when changed overlay line HTML is committed, directly affecting rendering latency and frame cadence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of whitespace glyphs across visible lines, after render mode filtering and the per-line stopRenderingLineAfter bound; batching changes DOM shape count from O(visible whitespace glyphs) to O(marker-bearing visible lines).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded and synchronous on the renderer UI path; visible lines are processed serially in one render pass, with no worker, queue, or backpressure boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no glyph cache. Each invalidated render recomputes visible-line markup, while ViewOverlayLine's _renderedContent comparison skips DOM replacement when the combined overlay HTML is unchanged. Newly exposed lines are cold; unchanged retained lines can avoid replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default SVG option, per-visible-line scan, overlay invalidation, HTML equality guard, DOM commit, and before/after node cardinality are directly established in repository code and the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact benefit varies with viewport size, whitespace density, browser SVG implementation, and hardware. The direction and cardinality reduction are established by the code and focused 1,000-space test; supplied measurements corroborate lower style time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. The change preserves per-marker geometry work but removes per-marker DOM-node fan-out on a synchronous rendering path, fixing a concrete rendering regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag or extend a selection through whitespace-dense text, including auto-scroll, while whitespace markers are visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cursor selection updates synchronously invalidate the selection-mode whitespace overlay; prepareRender scans visible lines and selected ranges, then changed line overlay HTML is committed before visual progress. In other whitespace modes, selection-overlay changes can still cause the shared per-line overlay subtree to be rebuilt with the existing whitespace markup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute whitespace overlay markup and replace changed shared overlay-line DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, every marker in each replaced line recreated an individual SVG child; after the diff, all markers on that line are represented by one child path. Path serialization still scales with selected/visible whitespace count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selection-triggered shared overlay replacement recreated one SVG shape element per whitespace marker; the diff reduces node construction and style work to one shape per affected line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The DOM update is on the drag-selection rendering path and contributes directly to input-to-frame latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Whitespace markers on affected visible lines multiplied by selection/render updates; after batching, DOM-node churn scales with affected lines rather than marker count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer-thread pass with serial visible-line processing; rapid pointer events are handled through the editor render scheduling, with no new concurrency introduced by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Whitespace path data is recomputed when the whitespace overlay itself invalidates in selection mode. The combined per-line HTML equality check avoids a DOM write for lines whose overlays remain byte-identical, but changed selections can alter the combined overlay string and replace the line subtree.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: selection invalidation and shared overlay-line string/DOM behavior are explicit in the code, and the diff's node-count reduction is exact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of affected lines and events depends on selection shape, pointer frequency, viewport, and whitespace mode. Controlled measurements in the PR metadata indicate substantial style-time reduction, but exact user impact varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. This is the main fixed scenario: batching removes repeated per-glyph DOM creation from a hot interactive path without increasing calls, concurrency, or retained lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run editor browser tests or process component screenshot fixtures.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test execution only; it is off all product startup, input, and rendering critical paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The test includes a synthetic line of 1,000 spaces to assert constant SVG element count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests run according to the existing test runner; the helper itself is synchronous and serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No runtime cache behavior changes. The added tests construct isolated overlays and DOM containers only during test execution; disposal is explicit and suite leak tracking owns created overlay registrations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new test file and markdown fixture are not imported by product runtime code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None relevant to product performance because these files execute only in tests or screenshot fixture processing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance regression; the test intentionally exercises scaling and the markdown change only updates fixture references.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff page. The runtime change fixes the default SVG whitespace renderer's per-glyph DOM-node fan-out by batching geometry into one path per marker-bearing line. No new high-confidence performance regression was found; no report_finding was submitted. Recorded the concrete shipped regression fix and its blamed introducing commit.
